### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **13** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/metadata`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/knowledge-memory`, `@objectstack/knowledge-pgvector`, `@objectstack/knowledge-turso`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/service-knowledge`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **301** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **34** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-core/src/index.ts`, `packages/plugins/knowledge-memory/README.md`, `packages/plugins/knowledge-pgvector/README.md`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**71** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e491fce2c70a67a92f2c40cb38e2f8b23af40ce4`.

⛔ **22** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **34** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-core/src/index.ts`, `packages/plugins/knowledge-memory/README.md`, `packages/plugins/knowledge-pgvector/README.md`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 56 pages)`, `VALIDATION_ERROR (literal, 39 pages)`, `/meta/:type/:name (route, 53 pages)`
- **47** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **197** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e491fce2c70a67a92f2c40cb38e2f8b23af40ce4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `be8795576ffda86fc8b6ad87928485a5130b4b0c` — the merge of head `45ed21271be3d1302a4e34d0c85e0da86fb8fccc` into base `e491fce2c70a67a92f2c40cb38e2f8b23af40ce4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin be8795576ffda86fc8b6ad87928485a5130b4b0c && git checkout be8795576ffda86fc8b6ad87928485a5130b4b0c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e491fce2c70a67a92f2c40cb38e2f8b23af40ce4 45ed21271be3d1302a4e34d0c85e0da86fb8fccc && git checkout -B drift-repro e491fce2c70a67a92f2c40cb38e2f8b23af40ce4 && git merge --no-ff 45ed21271be3d1302a4e34d0c85e0da86fb8fccc

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e491fce2c70a67a92f2c40cb38e2f8b23af40ce4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e491fce2c70a67a92f2c40cb38e2f8b23af40ce4` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ② Semver level

A release cut between the two would publish a skill that teaches shapes the same release refuses. #37310 lands before the next publish.

Seat questions:

1. Narrowing coverage. Yes. Every retired key has a tombstone, a retired-keys row, a pin row and a D2 conversion (`id`, `contentFields` renamed; `embedding`, `vectorStore`, `adapterConfig`, `refresh.cron` stripped, one notice each). 2. Ownership. Right, and consistent with ADR-0150 as amended on `main`. A code registration carries no package and `registerSource` refuses a body that names one; the package-less slot is shared with an environment item and the second arrival is refused `409` naming both doors; a package's source is a second slot under an index key no letter-led name can equal; a stored row's package is read from the row's binding, which the protocol states from the `package_id` column and never from a caller's body. The loader leaves a package-less row under a package-held name unserved and drops its index, which is point 7 as Step 0 answered it. The registry refuses a face two sources derive at the call, as the addendum's D6 bullet says (N3).
3. Security. The read side holds and is stricter than `main`: every hit is re-read as the caller, a hit with no record id or of an unregistered source is dropped, a hit naming another source than the one searched is dropped, and source admission is asked per caller on every search; the non-object pass that skipped the re-read is gone. No path was found by which a package or an author obtains another caller's hits, or by which a body claims a package's slot. Three findings on the authoring side, S1 to S3 in section ④; each is a pointer here and the detail is with the seat.
4. Generated and doc surfaces. `check:skill-refs` and `check:skill-top-level-keys` run in `Type Check · source gates`, success on the head; that conclusion is the verdict on byte-equality, and the two-line diff of `_index.md` is what the schema's new header and the module's removal imply. `skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md` changes by the `knowledgeSources` row alone, and its ceiling moves 6151 to 6156, pinned at the measurement, with both rulings quoted in the body as #32673 letter A requires. `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md` changes two keys of its compiled example: that is more than ruling A's "only that row", and it rests on card item 13's stated exception and on Tier H approval, not on ruling A. The ADR-0084 row is the row amend 7204020473 describes (AI, `ai`, 5, 高级, item 6's spelling) and is what `studioMenuPlacement.ts` mirrors (N2).
5. Changesets. As in ②.
6. Deviations. None undermines the evidence this record rests on. The first head's missing type check and suites were CI's to catch and CI caught them; the head reviewed here is green on all of them. The overlap check that exited 3 was re-run to the same answer and decides nothing about the tree. The long lock hold is an operations matter. One limit stands apart from the three: the pgvector live cells (74 skipped, `dropSource` among them) have not run on any head, because the job with a PostgreSQL service does not run on `pull_request`.

### ④ Design judgment

Schema files against K4, K5, K6 and the rulings: hold. The conversions are copy-on-write, ordered rename, rename, strip, and disjoint from the permission conversion that shares the major. The semantic entries say what a conversion cannot do. The registry, the loader, the reap guard and the three adapters agree with the contract sentences in `knowledge-adapter.ts` and `knowledge-service.ts` as read. The capability row and its default holders agree with ruling Q2 = B. The ADR and skill rows are as question 4 states.

S1 (should-fix) — Guard two judges less of a saved source than card item 8 and ADR-0161 K4 promise with "a field the author may not query". Pointer: `KnowledgeService.admitAuthoredSource` and `servedFieldsOf`, read against the keys `ObjectKnowledgeSourceSchema` declares and the module doc of `knowledge-source-admission.ts`. Security; mechanism withheld from this record.

S2 (should-fix) — `capabilities.ts` says every door that creates, changes or removes a `knowledge_source` asks `manage_knowledge_sources`, and the capability's published description says the same in fewer words. The doors the PR gates are the three the ruling names; the tree has others that reach the type on `manage_metadata` alone, and they are more than the "package install doors" the body declares. Either those doors ask it, or the sentence is narrowed and the remainder gets a carrier; which one is the maintainer's, since ruling Q2 names three doors. Security; detail with the seat.

S3 (should-fix) — `knowledge-source-save-admission.ts` states its fail direction as closed when the knowledge service cannot be resolved. That holds at the REST door. At the dispatcher door and the MCP draft door the resolver handed in cannot report that case, and the tests of those two doors pin only a verdict that throws. Pointer: the `resolveKnowledgeService` argument in `packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts` and `mcp-authoring.ts`, against `RestServer.resolveKnowledgeService`. Security; detail with the seat.

N1 (nit) — The changeset's "Removed exports" bullet names two schemas and "the rest of the embedding module". `FileKnowledgeSourceSchema`, `HttpKnowledgeSourceSchema`, `KnowledgeSourceKindSchema`, `VectorStoreProviderSchema` and the six types are not spelled, so an upgrader who greps the changelog for an import finds nothing.

N2 (nit) — ADR-0084 gains the row and nothing else, as the amend allows. The note under the table still counts "AI 4" and 33 entries at its dated reading, the fold sentence names `ai_context` alone, and item 6's heading names one type while two rows now point at it. A follow-up for the ADR's owner.

N3 (nit) — The PR body says two sources that derive one face are refused "at registration". The tree refuses at the call (`resolveSourceRef`), which is what ADR-0150 says. Its example, a package-less source named `crm-faq`, cannot parse: a name holds no `-`. Where the host cannot place a package's namespace the package's face is its bare name, and then that name answers `409` for both sources until the package is placed.

N4 (nit) — The `content` member pattern refuses `*` and admits the empty string, so `content: ['']` parses and indexes nothing for that member. The 18 shape admitted it too.

N5 (nit) — Each tombstone ends by sending the author to `os migrate meta --from 18`. For the only 18 instance there is, a registration in code, that command has nothing to walk. The D3 entry says the compiler and the parse carry it; the tombstone does not. The same entry does not say that a source whose 18 id began with an underscore keeps an index under the old key once it is renamed.

N6 (nit) — The ADR-0150 addendum asks this card to declare four narrowings "each with a count measured on the tree it lands on" (the install refusal inside a namespace, the name grammar, the `409` for a bare name two packages hold, the package-less row under a held name). The semantic entry covers the grammar and the code door; the counts are not stated on the PR.
